THE STRUCTURAL FINDING OF THIS DOSSIER. Adobe degraded its ARR disclosure twice in two years, timed with visible ARR deceleration. (1) Through Q4 FY2024 Adobe disclosed quarterly NET-NEW Digital Media ARR ($578M in Q4 FY2024, the last such disclosure) plus ending Digital Media ARR plus the Creative / Document Cloud split. (2) In FY2025 net-new ARR and the Creative/Document Cloud split were discontinued; only ending Digital Media ARR and its YoY growth remained (12.6% -> 12.1% -> 11.7% -> 11.5% across the four quarters). (3) From FY2026 Digital Media ARR itself was discontinued, and the FY2025 10-K states that effective Q1 FY2026 the three prior reportable segments (Digital Media, Digital Experience, Publishing and Advertising) are COMBINED INTO A SINGLE reportable segment; only Total Adobe ending ARR and its YoY growth remain. Adobe also revalued ending ARR at FY2025 year-end, raising Total Adobe ARR from $25.20B to $25.66B entering FY2026 (+$460M, attributed primarily to FX). Consequence: from FY2026 an outside investor can no longer verify whether the creative franchise specifically is losing customers. This drives kill criterion K-E (AMBER, already fired twice) and is the reason binding_constraint is COMPLETENESS rather than PRICE.
